title: Handling a sailing yacht under engine
lead: A sailing yacht under power has no brakes, steers only when water flows past the rudder and kicks sideways in reverse. Once you know why, manoeuvring in a tight harbour becomes calm and predictable.
description: How a single-engine sailing yacht handles under power: steering, the pivot point, prop wash, prop walk, going astern, stopping, the wind and turning in the boat's own length.
summary: The rudder works only with water flowing past it, from boat speed or from a burst of propeller wash.
Going ahead, the boat turns around a point near the mast, so the stern swings out wide: watch it in tight spaces.
In reverse, prop walk kicks the stern sideways, usually to port. Test it in open water, then use it.
Change gear only at idle, pause in neutral, and use short, firm bursts of power rather than long, gentle ones.
